html:
A Hindu monastic order and service organisation founded in Calcutta on 1 May 1897 by Swami Vivekananda, and named after his teacher, the mystic Ramakrishna. Its headquarters is at Belur Math on the Hooghly river near Kolkata.

Vivekananda returned from the West after his success at Chicago in 1893 determined to turn spiritual ideals into practical work. His motto for the order was "for one's own liberation and for the good of the world". Monks were to serve God in the poor and the sick. The mission began with famine and plague relief and went on to found schools, colleges, hospitals and rural programmes.

Its teaching is a modern form of Vedanta that sees all religions as true paths to one God, an idea Ramakrishna had lived out by practising several faiths. Belur Math's main temple mixes Hindu, Christian and Islamic forms to show this. The order now has branches across India and in many other countries, and it helped shape the idea of Hinduism as a world religion.
